active coefficients $c_{k-p},\ldots,c_k$. At the right endpoint $b$, the
caller supplies the last nonempty span and requests its left limit. At an
interior knot the half-open convention selects the span on its right.

The arithmetic mode is either exact real arithmetic or the operationwise
floating-point model of
[[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]].
The output is `success(value)`, `invalid-input`, or, in floating-point mode,
`range-failure(operation, r, j)`. The span search is supplied by the caller
and is not part of the evaluation loop.

1. If the indices, coefficient count, span, or query do not satisfy the
   input conditions, return `invalid-input`.
2. If $p=0$, return $c_k$ by copy.
3. Initialize $d_j^{(0)}=c_{k-p+j}$ for $0\le j\le p$.
4. For $r=1,\ldots,p$, and then $j=p,p-1,\ldots,r$, put
   $L=k-p+j$ and $U=k+1+j-r$. In exact mode set
   $\alpha=(x-t_L)/(t_U-t_L)$ and
   $d_j^{(r)}=(1-\alpha)d_{j-1}^{(r-1)}+\alpha d_j^{(r-1)}$.

   subtraction, then the division. If the rounded numerator is exact zero,

   Otherwise perform the complement subtraction, two multiplications and
   addition in that order, applying the model to each primitive operation.

   old $d_j^{(r-1)}$ until the update is complete.

weight therefore lies in $[0,1]$. When a span endpoint is requested as a
one-sided value, the same recurrence is evaluated at that endpoint with the
specified half-open or left-limit convention.

Let $p\in\mathbb N_0$, $n\ge p+1$, and $a<b$. A clamped knot vector is a nondecreasing finite sequence
$$\xi_1=\cdots=\xi_{p+1}=a<\xi_{p+2}\le\cdots\le\xi_n<\xi_{n+1}=\cdots=\xi_{n+p+1}=b,$$

Write $\mathcal P_p$ for the real polynomials of degree at most $p$. The degree-$p$ spline space $S_{p,\xi}$ consists of functions that restrict to a member of $\mathcal P_p$ on each nonempty knot interval and whose derivatives through order $p-\mu(\eta)$ agree across each interior knot $\eta$. For this piecewise definition, take knot cells left-closed and right-open; at a knot with no matching condition, the value is the one from the cell on its right, and at $b$ use the left limit. Thus the function value at a discontinuous knot is specified.

For each degree $d\in\{0,\ldots,p\}$, the functions $B_{j,d,\xi}$ are indexed by $1\le j\le n+p-d$. Set
$$B_{j,0,\xi}(x)=\mathbf 1_{[\xi_j,\xi_{j+1})}(x),\qquad 1\le j\le n+p.$$
For $1\le d\le p$ and $1\le j\le n+p-d$, define recursively
$$B_{j,d,\xi}(x)=\frac{x-\xi_j}{\xi_{j+d}-\xi_j}B_{j,d-1,\xi}(x)+\frac{\xi_{j+d+1}-x}{\xi_{j+d+1}-\xi_{j+1}}B_{j+1,d-1,\xi}(x),$$
where a term with zero denominator is defined to be zero. For every degree $d$ and every allowed index $j$, set $B_{j,d,\xi}(b)$ equal to its left limit. Let $p\in\mathbb N_0$ and let $\xi$ be a clamped knot vector as in [[def-b-spline-space-and-basis]]. The recursively defined degree-$p$ B-splines are nonnegative, are supported on $[\xi_j,\xi_{j+p+1}]$, and are piecewise polynomials of degree at most $p$. At a knot of multiplicity $\mu\le p$, each B-spline is $C^{p-\mu}$; multiplicity $p+1$ imposes no continuity requirement. Thus this degree reduction preserves the value at $x$.

Starting at $q=p$, repeat step 1.2. After $r-1$ reductions the active degree is $q=p-r+1$, and the coefficient indexed by $i=k-p+j$ has the weight $(x-t_{k-p+j})/(t_{k+1+j-r}-t_{k-p+j})$, exactly $\alpha_{j,r}$ in [F1]. Hence each algorithmic update is the coefficient collection in step 1.2 and preserves the spline value. After $p$ reductions the sole degree-zero indicator on the span is one, so the remaining coefficient $d_p^{(p)}$ equals $S(x)$. At $b$ equality on the last open span extends to the prescribed left limit.

At each precision, let the representable set, normal range, and unit roundoff be an instance of [[def-standard-relative-floating-point-model-and-unit-roundoff]] specialized to a finite binary format of integer precision $p\ge2$ and integer normal-exponent bounds $j_{\min}\le j\le j_{\max}$. Its normal values are $\pm m2^{j-p+1}$ for integers $2^{p-1}\le m<2^p$ and $j_{\min}\le j\le j_{\max}$, with $N_{\min}=2^{j_{\min}}$ and $N_{\max}=(2^p-1)2^{j_{\max}-p+1}$. The rounding rule is round-to-nearest, ties-to-even by the parity of the normalized significand. Each precision in a mixed-precision procedure has its own format, range, and valid unit-roundoff bound. On every real exact result that is zero or normal, $\operatorname{fl}$ uses this rule; every other nonzero exact result (subnormal or overflow), NaN, infinity, invalid operation, or division by zero returns range-failure. A real add, subtract, multiply, or divide is one rounded operation. For positive in-range $x$, $\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt{x})$ is correctly rounded to nearest, ties-to-even, and fails unless its result is positive and normal. A real fused multiply-add returns the correctly rounded value of the single exact expression $ab+c$; it is not two operations.

Complex addition and subtraction round real and imaginary components separately. A complex product (a+ib)(c+id) uses four rounded real products ac, bd, ad, bc, then rounded subtraction and addition, for six real operations. Conjugation and sign changes are exact. Scaling and division by a positive real scalar round each complex component separately; no other complex division primitive is used here.

A procedure succeeds only when each exact intermediate is zero or normal and every rounded output is finite; otherwise it returns the first range-failure with its operation or pivot index. For ku<1 write gamma_k=ku/(1-ku). This is a no-underflow success model, not the gradual-underflow model.

derivations.claim: At one blend let $\alpha\in[0,1]$ be the exact ratio. If its numerator is zero, the algorithm's exact-zero branch returns the left coefficient copy. Otherwise the two subtractions and division in [F2] give $\widehat\alpha=\alpha(1+\delta_1)(1+\delta_3)/(1+\delta_2)$, with $|\delta_i|\le u$ by [F1]. Hence $|\widehat\alpha-\alpha|\le\eta$. The complement subtraction gives $|\widehat\beta-(1-\alpha)|\le\eta+u(2+\eta)=e$, because $|1-\widehat\alpha|\le2+\eta$. Also $|\widehat\alpha|,|\widehat\beta|\le1+e=W$.

Write the two rounded products and final rounded sum as $\widehat y=\operatorname{fl}(\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\beta a)+\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\alpha b))$. Subtract the exact convex blend $(1-\alpha)a+\alpha b$. The coefficient differences contribute at most $e(|a|+|b|)$; the two product roundings contribute at most $uW(|a|+|b|)$; and the final addition contributes at most $u(1+u)W(|a|+|b|)$. Thus $|\widehat y-((1-\alpha)a+\alpha b)|\le E(|a|+|b|)$. If $M$ is the maximum magnitude in the preceding computed column, this is at most $2EM$. Since the exact blend is a convex combination, its magnitude is at most $M$, so the next computed column has maximum at most $(1+2E)M$.

Let $M_r$ be the maximum magnitude of the computed column after $r$ stages and let $\varepsilon_r$ be the maximum difference from the exact column. Step 1.2 gives $M_r\le(1+2E)^rM_0$. Since the exact weights are nonnegative and sum to one, the previous-column discrepancy contributes at most $\varepsilon_{r-1}$, while the local rounding contributes at most $2EM_{r-1}$. Therefore $\varepsilon_r\le\varepsilon_{r-1}+2E(1+2E)^{r-1}M_0$. Starting with $\varepsilon_0=0$ and summing this geometric series gives $\varepsilon_p\le((1+2E)^p-1)M_0$.
By [F3], the final exact column is $S(x)$; the final computed column is $\widehat S(x)$, and $M_0=\max_{k-p\le i\le k}|c_i|$. Substitution in step 2.1 proves the bound.

be $P_0,\ldots,P_{n-1}\in\mathbb R^d$. Let $k$ be a
nonempty span index with $t_k<u<t_{k+1}$, where $u$ is not already a knot.

[[def-b-spline-space-and-basis]], with endpoints $a=t_0$ and $b=t_{n+p}$.

$B_{i,q,v}=B_{i+1,q,\xi(v)}$. Let $k$ satisfy $t_k<t_{k+1}$, let
$t_k<u<t_{k+1}$, and obtain $t'$ by inserting $u$ between $t_k$ and
$t_{k+1}$. For $0\le q\le p$, define
$$\lambda_i^{(q)}=\begin{cases}1,&i\le k-q,\\\frac{u-t_i}{t_{i+q}-t_i},&k-q+1\le i\le k,\\0,&i\ge k+1.\end{cases}$$

This also covers $p=0$, when the blend range is empty. Let $a=x_0<x_1<\cdots<x_m=b$, with $m\ge1$, let
$y_0,\ldots,y_m\in\mathbb R$, and prescribe endpoint slopes
$\sigma_a,\sigma_b\in\mathbb R$. A **clamped cubic spline interpolant**
for these data is a function $s\in C^2([a,b])$ whose restriction to every
$[x_i,x_{i+1}]$ is a polynomial of degree at most three, which satisfies
$s(x_i)=y_i$ for every $i$, and which satisfies
$s'(a)=\sigma_a$ and $s'(b)=\sigma_b$.

Here $C^2$ means that the function and its first two derivatives are
continuous on $[a,b]$, with one-sided derivatives at the endpoints. This
uses the piecewise-cubic convention in
[[def-natural-cubic-spline]] and replaces its natural endpoint-curvature
conditions by prescribed endpoint slopes. It does not alter the natural

in [[def-b-spline-space-and-basis]], so $t_0\le\cdots\le t_{n+p}$ with
$n\ge p+1$. Let $p\in\mathbb N_0$, $d\in\mathbb N$, and let the controls
be $P_0,\ldots,P_{n-1}\in\mathbb R^d$. Let $k$ be a
nonempty span index with $t_k<u<t_{k+1}$, where $u$ is not already a knot.
Insert $u$ between $t_k$ and $t_{k+1}$ to obtain $t'$. The output controls
$Q_0,\ldots,Q_n$ are defined by

$$Q_i=\begin{cases}P_i,&0\le i\le k-p,\\\alpha_iP_i+(1-\alpha_i)P_{i-1},&k-p+1\le i\le k,\\P_{i-1},&k+1\le i\le n,\end{cases}\qquad\alpha_i=\frac{u-t_i}{t_{i+p}-t_i}.$$

derivations.claim: Since the knot vector is clamped, a nonempty span index satisfies $p\le k\le n-1$. The insertion map is $t'_j=t_j$ for $j\le k$, $t'_{k+1}=u$, and $t'_j=t_{j-1}$ for $j\ge k+2$. For $q=0$, $\lambda_i^{(0)}=1$ when $i\le k$ and $0$ when $i\ge k+1$. Every old half-open degree-zero cell other than $[t_k,t_{k+1})$ is unchanged or shifts by one index; the affected cell splits as $[t_k,u)\cup[u,t_{k+1})$. Thus the indicator identity holds for all degree-zero indices, including zero-length repeated-knot cells; at $u$ the right cell supplies the value. The value at $b$ follows by the stipulated left limit.

Fix $1\le q\le p$ and assume the identity holds in degree $q-1$. For $x\in[a,b)$, write $A_i=(x-t_i)/(t_{i+q}-t_i)$ and $D_i=(t_{i+q+1}-x)/(t_{i+q+1}-t_{i+1})$, with any zero-denominator term defined as zero as in [F1]; define $A'_i,D'_i$ using $t'$. Expanding the old recurrence and applying the degree-$(q-1)$ identity gives the coefficient triple $(A_i\lambda_i^{(q-1)},\ A_i(1-\lambda_{i+1}^{(q-1)})+D_i\lambda_{i+1}^{(q-1)},\ D_i(1-\lambda_{i+2}^{(q-1)}))$ on $B'_{i,q-1},B'_{i+1,q-1},B'_{i+2,q-1}$. Expanding the proposed refined expression gives $(\lambda_i^{(q)}A'_i,\ \lambda_i^{(q)}D'_i+(1-\lambda_{i+1}^{(q)})A'_{i+1},\ (1-\lambda_{i+1}^{(q)})D'_{i+1})$. It remains to prove these three coefficient equalities for $k-q\le i\le k$.

For the first coefficient, at $i=k-q$ both $\lambda_i^{(q-1)}$ and $\lambda_i^{(q)}$ are $1$, and the insertion map gives $t'_i=t_i$ and $t'_{i+q}=t_{i+q}=t_k$. Hence $A'_i=A_i$; if this common denominator is zero, both terms are zero by [F1]. For $k-q+1\le i\le k$, put $a=t_i$, $b=t_{i+q}$ and $v=t'_{i+q}$. Then $a\le t_k<u<b$. At the lower index $i=k-q+1$, $v=u$ and $\lambda_i^{(q-1)}=1=(u-a)/(v-a)$. At higher indices in this range, the definition gives the same ratio because $v=t_{i+q-1}$. All denominators here are positive, and $A_i\lambda_i^{(q-1)}=((x-a)/(b-a))((u-a)/(v-a))=((u-a)/(b-a))((x-a)/(v-a))=\lambda_i^{(q)}A'_i$. This also covers $q=1$, where the lower-degree weight is the degree-zero value $1$.

For the last coefficient, first take $k-q\le i\le k-1$ and put $c=t_{i+1}$, $d=t_{i+q+1}$, and $w=t'_{i+2}$. Then $c\le t_k<u<d$ and $w\le t_k$ for $i\le k-2$, while $w=u$ for $i=k-1$. In both cases $d-c>0$, $d-w>0$, and $\lambda_{i+2}^{(q-1)}=(u-w)/(d-w)$ (zero in the case $w=u$). Consequently $1-\lambda_{i+2}^{(q-1)}=(d-u)/(d-w)$, $1-\lambda_{i+1}^{(q)}=(d-u)/(d-c)$, and $D'_{i+1}=(d-x)/(d-w)$, while $D_i=(d-x)/(d-c)$. Multiplying proves $D_i(1-\lambda_{i+2}^{(q-1)})=(1-\lambda_{i+1}^{(q)})D'_{i+1}$. At $i=k$, both $\lambda_{k+2}^{(q-1)}$ and $\lambda_{k+1}^{(q)}$ are zero, and the insertion map gives $D'_{k+1}=D_k$. If their common denominator is zero, both terms are zero by [F1]; otherwise equality follows from the identical numerator and denominator.

For the middle coefficient at the lower boundary $i=k-q$, put $c=t_{i+1}$ and $d=t_{k+1}$. Here $\lambda_i^{(q)}=1$ and $\lambda_{i+1}^{(q-1)}=1$, so the old middle coefficient is $D_i=(d-x)/(d-c)$. Also $1-\lambda_{i+1}^{(q)}=(d-u)/(d-c)$, $D'_i=(u-x)/(u-c)$, and $A'_{i+1}=(x-c)/(u-c)$. All displayed denominators are positive, and the new middle coefficient is $\lambda_i^{(q)}D'_i+(1-\lambda_{i+1}^{(q)})A'_{i+1}=(u-x)/(u-c)+(d-u)(x-c)/((d-c)(u-c))=(d-x)/(d-c)=D_i$. The omitted old term $A_i(1-\lambda_{i+1}^{(q-1)})$ is zero even if $A_i$ has zero denominator, because [F1] defines that term as zero and its multiplier is zero. At the upper boundary $i=k$, $\lambda_{i+1}^{(q-1)}=\lambda_{i+1}^{(q)}=0$, so the old middle coefficient is $A_i$. Put $a=t_k$ and $b=t_{k+q}$; then $a<u<b$. The insertion map gives $\lambda_i^{(q)}=(u-a)/(b-a)$, $D'_i=(b-x)/(b-u)$, and $A'_{i+1}=(x-u)/(b-u)$. Therefore the new middle coefficient is $\lambda_i^{(q)}D'_i+(1-\lambda_{i+1}^{(q)})A'_{i+1}=((u-a)(b-x)+(b-a)(x-u))/((b-a)(b-u))=(x-a)/(b-a)=A_i$. The old term $D_i\lambda_{i+1}^{(q-1)}$ is zero without division by its denominator. For the strict interior $k-q+1\le i\le k-1$, which is empty if $q=1$, put $a=t_i$, $c=t_{i+1}$, $b=t_{i+q}$, and $d=t_{i+q+1}$. The insertion span gives $a\le c\le t_k<u<t_{k+1}\le b\le d$, so every denominator below is positive. The old and refined middle coefficients are respectively $((x-a)(b-u)/(b-a)+(d-x)(u-c)/(d-c))/(b-c)$ and $((u-a)(b-x)/(b-a)+(d-u)(x-c)/(d-c))/(b-c)$. Their first numerator terms differ by $x-u$, since $(x-a)(b-u)-(u-a)(b-x)=(b-a)(x-u)$. Their second numerator terms differ by $u-x$, since $(d-x)(u-c)-(d-u)(x-c)=(d-c)(u-x)$. Thus their sum is equal. These lower, strict-interior, and upper cases prove the middle coefficient identity.

For $i<k-q$, both weights in the refinement formula are $1$, and the complete local knot list used by $B_{i,q,t}$ is unchanged in $t'$, so the recursively defined basis function is unchanged. For $i\ge k+1$, both weights are $0$, and the local knot list shifts by one, giving $B_{i,q,t}=B_{i+1,q,t'}$. For the transition range, steps 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3 establish all three coefficients in step 2.1, so the Cox–de Boor expansions agree. Induction from the degree-zero base in step 1.1 proves the formula for every $q\le p$. The argument is pointwise on $[a,b)$ under the right-cell convention, including repeated knots; taking left limits gives the equality at $b$. No continuity at knots is assumed.

Use one binary floating-point format from
[[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]
with round-to-nearest, ties-to-even, a known rational unit roundoff
$0<u\le1/4$, and the model's normal-or-zero success rule. Inputs are
$r\ge2$ finite stored real knots $x_1<\cdots<x_r$ and finite stored real
values $y_1,\ldots,y_r$. These stored numbers are the exact interpolation
data; no unrecorded perturbation of the data is included. Write
$h_i=x_{i+1}-x_i$ for their exact rational differences. If a constant $2$
or $6$ needed by the selected branch is not representable as a finite normal
number, return `input-format-failure`. Arithmetic statuses below report the
first failing operation in the specified order. This algorithm makes no
claim that floating-point success is automatic.

If $r=2$, return `success` with endpoint second derivatives
$\widehat M_1=\widehat M_2=0$ and error certificate $B=0$. The corresponding
piece is the exact straight line. For $r\ge3$, put $n=r-2$ and return
`certificate-parameter-failure` unless $(n-1)u<1$.

For $r\ge3$, assemble stored widths and secant slopes in increasing
$i=1,\ldots,r-1$: compute
$\widehat h_i=\operatorname{fl}(x_{i+1}-x_i)$,
$a_i=\operatorname{fl}(y_{i+1}-y_i)$, and
$q_i=\operatorname{fl}(a_i/\widehat h_i)$, in that order. At the first
failed operation return `assembly-range-failure(i,operation)`. Successful
width subtraction gives $\widehat h_i>0$. In increasing $k=1,\ldots,n$,
for the row corresponding to knot $x_{k+1}$ compute
$$
s_k=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat h_k+\widehat h_{k+1}),\quad d_k=\operatorname{fl}(2s_k),\quad t_k=\operatorname{fl}(q_{k+1}-q_k),\quad f_k=\operatorname{fl}(6t_k)
$$
in that order. Copy $c_k=\widehat h_{k+1}$ for $k<n$. On failure return
`assembly-range-failure(k,operation)`. Let $T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$
have diagonal $d_k$, adjacent off-diagonal entries $c_k$, and zero entries
elsewhere; represent it by these three diagonals, not a dense array. Let the
stored right-hand side be $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_n)^T$.

Factor $T$ with a real lower bidiagonal factor, stored as diagonal
$\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n$ and subdiagonal $e_1,\ldots,e_{n-1}$. For
$k=1,\ldots,n$ in order, set $p_1=d_1$ by exact copy; for $k>1$ compute
$\zeta_k=\operatorname{fl}(e_{k-1}e_{k-1})$ and
$p_k=\operatorname{fl}(d_k-\zeta_k)$. If either operation fails, return
`factor-range-failure(k,operation)`. If the resulting $p_k$ fails the
published positive-normal pivot test of
[[alg-rounded-cholesky-with-failure-status]], return `invalid-pivot(k,p_k)`.
Otherwise compute
$\ell_k=\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt{p_k})$; on failure or a nonpositive or
nonnormal result return `factor-range-failure(k,operation)`. For $k<n$ compute
$e_k=\operatorname{fl}(c_k/\ell_k)$ and return the same indexed factor
status on failure.

Solve $Lz=f$ by forward substitution in increasing index order: set
$z_1=\operatorname{fl}(f_1/\ell_1)$; for $k>1$, compute
$a=\operatorname{fl}(e_{k-1}z_{k-1})$,
$b=\operatorname{fl}(f_k-a)$, and $z_k=\operatorname{fl}(b/\ell_k)$.
Solve $L^T\widehat m=z$ in decreasing order: set
$\widehat m_n=\operatorname{fl}(z_n/\ell_n)$; for $k<n$, compute
$a=\operatorname{fl}(e_k\widehat m_{k+1})$,
$b=\operatorname{fl}(z_k-a)$, and
$\widehat m_k=\operatorname{fl}(b/\ell_k)$. At the first failed operation
return `solve-range-failure(direction,k,operation)`. These are separate
multiply, subtract, and divide operations; no fused multiply-add is used.
Set $\widehat M_1=\widehat M_r=0$ and copy the interior vector
$\widehat M_{k+1}=\widehat m_k$.

Compute the rounded residual in increasing row order. Within row $k$, form
the products $T_{kj}\widehat m_j$ for existing columns $j$ in increasing
column order, and add them sequentially from an exact zero accumulator to
obtain $\widehat v_k$. Then compute
$\widehat w_k=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat v_k-f_k)$. Return the first
`residual-range-failure(k,j,operation)` if any operation fails. Structural
zero entries are omitted; all included products, additions, and the final
subtraction use the operationwise model.

The certificate calculations that follow are exact rational arithmetic on
the finite binary values and the rational $u$; they are not rounded
floating-point calculations. Define
$$
F_1=\sum_{k=1}^n|d_k|+2\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}|c_k|,\quad X_1=\sum_{k=1}^n|\widehat m_k|,\quad Y_1=\sum_{k=1}^n|f_k|,\quad V_1=\sum_{k=1}^n|\widehat v_k|,\quad W_1=\sum_{k=1}^n|\widehat w_k|
$$
and
$$
g_n=\frac{1+6u}{1-(n-1)u}-1,\qquad C=W_1+g_nF_1X_1+u(V_1+Y_1).
$$
Form the exact natural-cubic matrix $A$ and right-hand side $b$ for the
original stored data as in
[[thm-natural-cubic-interpolant-exists-uniquely-at-distinct-knots]]:
$A_{kk}=2(h_k+h_{k+1})$, $A_{k,k+1}=A_{k+1,k}=h_{k+1}$, and
$b_k=6((y_{k+2}-y_{k+1})/h_{k+1}-(y_{k+1}-y_k)/h_k)$, with only existing
interior entries included; represent $A$ by its three diagonals and compute
the following row quantities as a stream, without allocating dense matrices.
Compute
$$
\alpha=\max_k\sum_j|A_{kj}-T_{kj}|,\quad \beta=\max_k|b_k-f_k|,\quad Q=\max_k|\widehat m_k|,\quad \delta=\min_{1\le k\le n}(h_k+h_{k+1}),\quad H=\max_{1\le i<r}h_i,
$$
and
$$
B=\frac{H^2}{8\delta}(C+\alpha Q+\beta).
$$
All denominators are positive: $h_i>0$, $\delta>0$, and
$1-(n-1)u>0$. Return `success(\widehat M,C,\alpha,\beta,B)`. If a
resource-limited implementation cannot complete the exact rational
certificate, it may return `certificate-resource-failure`, which carries no
certified $B$.

For $r\ge3$, associate to the returned vector $\widehat M$ the piecewise
cubic reconstruction on each $[x_i,x_{i+1}]$ given by
$$
\widehat s_i(x)=\frac{\widehat M_i(x_{i+1}-x)^3+\widehat M_{i+1}(x-x_i)^3}{6h_i}+\left(y_i-\frac{\widehat M_i h_i^2}{6}\right)\frac{x_{i+1}-x}{h_i}+\left(y_{i+1}-\frac{\widehat M_{i+1}h_i^2}{6}\right)\frac{x-x_i}{h_i}.
$$
This reconstruction interpolates the stored data and need not be $C^1$ at an interior knot;
it is a piecewise cubic reconstruction, not necessarily a natural spline.
The certificate concerns exact evaluation of these pieces. Any floating-point
evaluation of them needs a separate piece-evaluation error allowance.

At each precision, let the representable set, normal range, and unit roundoff be an instance of [[def-standard-relative-floating-point-model-and-unit-roundoff]] specialized to a finite binary format of integer precision $p\ge2$ and integer normal-exponent bounds $j_{\min}\le j\le j_{\max}$. Its normal values are $\pm m2^{j-p+1}$ for integers $2^{p-1}\le m<2^p$ and $j_{\min}\le j\le j_{\max}$, with $N_{\min}=2^{j_{\min}}$ and $N_{\max}=(2^p-1)2^{j_{\max}-p+1}$. The rounding rule is round-to-nearest, ties-to-even by the parity of the normalized significand. Each precision in a mixed-precision procedure has its own format, range, and valid unit-roundoff bound. On every real exact result that is zero or normal, $\operatorname{fl}$ uses this rule; every other nonzero exact result (subnormal or overflow), NaN, infinity, invalid operation, or division by zero returns range-failure. A real add, subtract, multiply, or divide is one rounded operation. For positive in-range $x$, $\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt{x})$ is correctly rounded to nearest, ties-to-even, and fails unless its result is positive and normal. A real fused multiply-add returns the correctly rounded value of the single exact expression $ab+c$; it is not two operations.

Complex addition and subtraction round real and imaginary components separately. A complex product (a+ib)(c+id) uses four rounded real products ac, bd, ad, bc, then rounded subtraction and addition, for six real operations. Conjugation and sign changes are exact. Scaling and division by a positive real scalar round each complex component separately; no other complex division primitive is used here.

A procedure succeeds only when each exact intermediate is zero or normal and every rounded output is finite; otherwise it returns the first range-failure with its operation or pivot index. For ku<1 write gamma_k=ku/(1-ku). This is a no-underflow success model, not the gradual-underflow model.

Input a Hermitian positive-definite matrix $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, $n\ge1$, whose real and imaginary components are in the floating-point system, using the convention of [[def-cholesky-factorisation-with-positive-diagonal]]; real matrices are included. Initialize every entry of $\widehat L$ to zero. Process columns $j=1,\ldots,n$ in increasing order. For the diagonal, initialize $s=0$ and, for $k=1,\ldots,j-1$ in increasing order, compute
$$r_k=\operatorname{fl}(\Re(\widehat l_{jk})^2),\quad t_k=\operatorname{fl}(\Im(\widehat l_{jk})^2),\quad q_k=\operatorname{fl}(r_k+t_k),\quad s=\operatorname{fl}(s+q_k),$$
in that order. Then compute $p_j=\operatorname{fl}(a_{jj}-s)$. If an operation fails, or if $p_j$ is not positive and normal, return `failure` with pivot $j$ and the first failing operation location. Otherwise compute $\widehat l_{jj}=\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt{p_j})$; if it is not positive and normal, return `failure` at pivot $j$.

For each $i=j+1,\ldots,n$ in increasing order, initialize the complex accumulator $c_{ij}=0$. For $k=1,\ldots,j-1$ in increasing order, compute the complex product $w_{ik}=\widehat l_{ik}\overline{\widehat l_{jk}}$ using exactly the six real operations of the complex-product convention in [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]], then update
$$\Re(c_{ij})\gets\operatorname{fl}(\Re(c_{ij})+\Re(w_{ik})),\qquad \Im(c_{ij})\gets\operatorname{fl}(\Im(c_{ij})+\Im(w_{ik})).$$
After this dot product, compute $r_{ij}=a_{ij}-c_{ij}$ by one rounded real subtraction for each component, then compute each component of $\widehat l_{ij}=r_{ij}/\widehat l_{jj}$ by one rounded real division. The empty dot product is zero. On any failure return `failure` with pivot $j$ and its first failing operation location (stage, column, row, inner index, component, and operation where applicable), with the diagonal and row loops ordered as stated. If all columns finish, return `success(\widehat L)`. By [[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]], exact positive definiteness ensures an exact factor exists, but does not ensure the rounded algorithm succeeds.

Let $R\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be upper triangular with stored floating-point entries and nonzero diagonal, and let $y\in\mathbb R^n$ have stored floating-point entries, where $n\ge1$ and $(n+3)u<1$. Use the operationwise arithmetic model of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]] at unit roundoff $u$. Compute descending substitution by the sequential rounded dot $s_i=\operatorname{fl}(\sum_{j>i}R_{ij}\widehat x_j)$ (empty sum zero), $t_i=\operatorname{fl}(y_i-s_i)$, and $\widehat x_i=\operatorname{fl}(t_i/R_{ii})$. Assume each exact intermediate is zero or normal and each rounded result is finite, so every operation succeeds under that model. Then there is upper triangular $\Delta R$ with
$$(R+\Delta R)\widehat x=y,\qquad |\Delta R|\le\gamma_{n+3}|R|,\qquad \|\Delta R\|_F\le\gamma_{n+3}\|R\|_F.$$
In particular $\widehat x=0$ forces $y=0$. Forward substitution has the transposed conclusion.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $A=A^*$ be positive definite in $\mathbb C^{n\times n}$. Suppose the rounded Cholesky algorithm succeeds with $\widehat L$. Put $m=20n+20$ and $g=\gamma_m=\frac{m u}{1-m u}$; assume $m u<1/5$. For $E=\widehat L\widehat L^*-A$, which is Hermitian, and with $|M|$ denoting entrywise absolute value for matrices,
$$|E|\le100g\,|\widehat L|\,|\widehat L|^*\quad\hbox{entrywise},\qquad \|E\|_F\le100g\|\widehat L\|_F^2,\qquad \|E\|_2\le100g\|\widehat L\|_F^2.$$
Thus $c_n(u)u=\frac{100m u}{1-m u}$. If also $100\sqrt n\,g\le1/2$, then
$$\|E\|_F\le200\sqrt n\,g\|A\|_F,\qquad \|E\|_2\le200\sqrt n\,g\|A\|_F.$$
These bounds apply on success only; positive definiteness does not guarantee rounded success.

Let $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$, $x\in\mathbb F^n$, $y\in\mathbb F^m$ have stored real or complex entries, with $m,n\ge1$. Use the operationwise arithmetic model, successful sequential dot products, and $0<u<1$ with $(\max(m,n)-1)u<1$. Define
$$g_k=\frac{1+6u}{1-(k-1)u}-1,\qquad F=\|A\|_F,\quad X=\|x\|_2,\quad Y=\|y\|_2.$$
For $\widehat v=\operatorname{fl}(Ax)$ and $\widehat w=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat v-y)$, put $V=g_nFX$ and $W=V+u(\|\widehat v\|_2+Y)$. Then
$$\|\widehat w-(Ax-y)\|_2\le W.$$
For a stored real $\lambda>0$, also compute $\widehat z=\operatorname{fl}(A^*\widehat w)$, $\widehat l=\operatorname{fl}(\lambda x)$ and $\widehat r=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat z+\widehat l)$, rounding scalar multiplication componentwise. The exact intended normal residual $r=A^*(Ax-y)+\lambda x$ satisfies
$$\|\widehat r-r\|_2\le\rho:=FW+g_mF\|\widehat w\|_2+u\lambda X+u(\|\widehat z\|_2+\|\widehat l\|_2).$$
Norms in these certificates mean exact norms or certified upper bounds. Uncontrolled rounding of the certificate itself is not authorized. The linear bound applies columnwise to certify $\|I-AB\|_2\le\|I-AB\|_F$ from stored basis-solve columns $B$.

Fix an initialized finite state and an ordered list of $M\ge0$ instructions, followed by a specified completion return. Each instruction reads only initialized data and deterministically either produces the next finite state or returns a specified early status in finite time. There are no backward jumps. Then execution terminates at the first early return, if any, or at the completion return, after at most $M$ attempted instructions. A finite nesting of counted loops with bounds fixed by the finite input has the same property whenever unrolling the loops gives such a list.

In particular, consider $d\ge0$ levels containing $2^{d-\ell}$ addition instructions at level $\ell=1,\ldots,d$, with each addition returning a rounded value or immediate failure. A successful execution attempts exactly $2^d-1$ additions; every execution attempts at most $2^d-1$. For $d=0$ there are no additions. These conclusions assert finite execution, not arithmetic success or accuracy.

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, let $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let
$A=(a_{ij})\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$. The **Frobenius norm** of $A$ is

$$\lVert A\rVert_F\;:=\;\Bigl(\,\sum_{i<m}\sum_{j<n}|a_{ij}|^{2}\Bigr)^{1/2},$$

where $|\cdot|$ is the absolute value on $\mathbb R$
([[def-abs-value]]) for $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ and the modulus on $\mathbb C$
([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]) for
$\mathbb F=\mathbb C$, and the outer power is the nonnegative real square root.

**The displayed quantity is a norm.** Regard $A$ as the element of the
coordinate space $\mathbb F^{mn}$ whose $j+in$-th entry is $a_{ij}$. The
standard coordinate inner product of [[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]
satisfies $\langle A,A\rangle=\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}\overline{a_{ij}}$, which equals
$\sum_{i,j}|a_{ij}|^{2}$ because $z\overline z=|z|^{2}$
([[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]). Thus $\lVert A\rVert_F$ is
exactly the inner-product norm of [[def-inner-product-norm]] evaluated at $A$,
and the three norm axioms hold for $\lVert\cdot\rVert_F$ because they hold for
every inner-product norm. For real matrices the same sum is
$\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}^{2}$, since $|x|^{2}=x^{2}$ for real $x$ by the two cases of
[[def-abs-value]].

The Frobenius norm is the Euclidean norm of the full entry list, not the
largest factor by which the matrix stretches a single vector. It can coincide
with an induced $2$-norm in one-row or one-column cases, but in general it is a
different matrix norm from the induced operator norms used on this page. Its
relation to the spectral norm, its unitary invariance and its singular-value
formula are
[[thm-spectral-and-frobenius-norms-are-unitarily-invariant-with-singular-value-formulas-and-rank-comparison]].

For a vector $v$ in a real or complex inner product space, define its **inner-product norm** by

$$\lVert v\rVert:=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}.$$

Positive definiteness in [[def-inner-product-space]] makes the radicand a nonnegative real, and [[thm-nth-roots-exist]] supplies its unique nonnegative square root. The notation therefore defines one real number $\lVert v\rVert\ge0$. Its norm axioms are established in [[cor-triangle-inequality-for-inner-product-norm]].

For $x,y\in\mathbb R^n$ and $z,w\in\mathbb C^n$, the formulas

$$\langle x,y\rangle_{\mathbb R^n}=\sum_{k<n}x_ky_k,\qquad \langle z,w\rangle_{\mathbb C^n}=\sum_{k<n}z_k\overline{w_k}$$

define inner products, linear in the first argument. At $n=0$, the unique pairing on the zero space is an inner product.

derivations.claim: Each successful width subtraction has exact positive input difference, so by [F2] its stored result $\widehat h_i$ is positive. Write $S_k=\widehat h_k+\widehat h_{k+1}$. The successful rounding of its sum and multiplication by $2$ gives $d_k\ge2(1-u)^2S_k\ge(9/8)S_k>S_k$. Row $k$'s off-diagonal absolute sum is at most $S_k$: it contains only some of the positive entries $\widehat h_k,\widehat h_{k+1}$, and for $n=1$ it is zero. For any real nonzero vector $v$, applying $2c_kv_kv_{k+1}\ge-|c_k|(v_k^2+v_{k+1}^2)$ to each adjacent term yields $v^TTv\ge\sum_k(d_k-\sum_{j\ne k}|T_{kj}|)v_k^2>0$. Hence every successfully assembled $T$ is real SPD.

In the dense Cholesky recurrence of [F3], induction over columns shows that $\widehat L_{ij}=0$ for $i>j+1$: the input matrix is tridiagonal, and in each such row the prior-column products and input entry are zero. At $k=1$ the diagonal square-sum is empty, so its pivot is copied as $p_1=d_1$, exactly as in the local algorithm. For $k>1$, the only possible nonzero term in the dense diagonal square-sum is $e_{k-1}^2$; the remaining zero products, additions and subtractions are exact and cannot fail under [F2]. Thus the dense pivot is exactly the specialized $p_k$, followed by the same square root and positive-normal test. For the first subdiagonal, the dense dot product has only the input $c_k$ after its exact zero terms, so the update is exactly $\operatorname{fl}(c_k/\ell_k)$. Every lower entry beyond that subdiagonal is exactly zero. This induction proves equality of all stored factor entries and all potentially failing operations. The forward and backward dense triangular recurrences likewise have only the single adjacent product; all other terms are exact zeros. Therefore the specialized solve outputs equal the published substitutions.

Let $r_*=T\widehat m-f$ be the exact residual. The algorithm computes the same sparse sequential products and subtraction as the dense dot product in [F6], with only exact-zero products and additions omitted. By [F2], a zero product is exact and adding zero to a stored normal value or zero is also exact, so the sparse accumulation is identical to the dense one. Thus [F6] gives $\|\widehat w-r_*\|_2\le g_n\|T\|_F\|\widehat m\|_2+u(\|\widehat v\|_2+\|f\|_2)$. By [F9] and [F10], the Euclidean norm is the square root of the sum of squared coordinates, so each coordinate magnitude is at most that norm and $\|v\|_2\le\sum_k|v_k|$; the latter follows by squaring, since all cross terms are nonnegative. By [F8], the same argument on the finite entry list gives $\|T\|_F\le\sum_{i,j}|T_{ij}|=F_1$. The definitions in [F1] therefore imply $\|\widehat w\|_2\le W_1$, $\|\widehat m\|_2\le X_1$, $\|\widehat v\|_2\le V_1$, and $\|f\|_2\le Y_1$. The coordinate bound also gives $\|r_*\|_\infty\le\|r_*\|_2$, whence $\|r_*\|_\infty\le\|r_* -\widehat w\|_2+\|\widehat w\|_2\le C$. Setting $e=r_*$ gives the stated exact right-hand-side perturbation without division by a solution or residual norm.

If $(n+3)u<1$, apply [F4] to each successful triangular substitution from step 1.2. It gives $D_1,D_2$ with $(\widehat L+D_1)z=f$ and $(\widehat L^T+D_2)\widehat m=z$ and the stated entrywise bounds; since $\widehat L$ is bidiagonal, those bounds force $D_1,D_2$ to be bidiagonal as well. Under the distinct condition $(20n+20)u<1/5$, step 1.1 and [F5] give $E=\widehat L\widehat L^T-T$ and the stated factor bound. Substituting the second triangular equation into the first gives $(\widehat L+D_1)(\widehat L^T+D_2)\widehat m=f$. Expanding the product and using $\widehat L\widehat L^T=T+E$ yields $(T+J)\widehat m=f$. Entrywise submultiplicativity and the bounds on $D_1,D_2,E$ give the displayed bound for $J$. The conditional Frobenius estimate is exactly the further norm consequence in [F5], with the norm convention in [F8].

Put $n=r-2$. Assembly makes a fixed number of floating-point operations per each of the $r-1$ intervals and $n$ rows. Factorization, each substitution and residual evaluation visit $n$ rows, with at most a fixed number of operations per row because a tridiagonal row has at most three nonzero entries. The exact-certificate scan likewise visits $r-1$ intervals and $n$ rows; each contributes a fixed number of rational operations and comparisons to the sums, row discrepancies, and extrema, followed by a fixed number to form $B$. Thus the floating-point and exact rational operation counts are $O(r)$. The algorithm stores only input and output vectors, the bidiagonal factor, the three diagonals of $T$ and $A$, and a fixed number of rational accumulators; row discrepancies can be computed as they are scanned, so storage is $O(r)$ scalars and $O(r)$ rationals. Every loop has a finite index range and every floating-point instruction returns or its first failure. The certificate denominators $h_i$, $\delta$, and $1-(n-1)u$ are positive, so each exact rational operation has finite inputs and is defined. [F7] therefore gives termination; if a resource limit prevents completion of the exact certificate, the algorithm returns its separate failure status and no $B$. No rational bit-complexity bound follows.

citations.quote:
Use one binary floating-point format from
[[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]
with round-to-nearest, ties-to-even, a known rational unit roundoff
$0<u\le1/4$, and the model's normal-or-zero success rule. Inputs are
$r\ge2$ finite stored real knots $x_1<\cdots<x_r$ and finite stored real
values $y_1,\ldots,y_r$. These stored numbers are the exact interpolation
data; no unrecorded perturbation of the data is included. Write
$h_i=x_{i+1}-x_i$ for their exact rational differences. If a constant $2$
or $6$ needed by the selected branch is not representable as a finite normal
number, return `input-format-failure`. Arithmetic statuses below report the
first failing operation in the specified order. This algorithm makes no
claim that floating-point success is automatic.

If $r=2$, return `success` with endpoint second derivatives
$\widehat M_1=\widehat M_2=0$ and error certificate $B=0$. The corresponding
piece is the exact straight line. For $r\ge3$, put $n=r-2$ and return
`certificate-parameter-failure` unless $(n-1)u<1$.

For $r\ge3$, assemble stored widths and secant slopes in increasing
$i=1,\ldots,r-1$: compute
$\widehat h_i=\operatorname{fl}(x_{i+1}-x_i)$,
$a_i=\operatorname{fl}(y_{i+1}-y_i)$, and
$q_i=\operatorname{fl}(a_i/\widehat h_i)$, in that order. At the first
failed operation return `assembly-range-failure(i,operation)`. Successful
width subtraction gives $\widehat h_i>0$. In increasing $k=1,\ldots,n$,
for the row corresponding to knot $x_{k+1}$ compute
$$
s_k=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat h_k+\widehat h_{k+1}),\quad d_k=\operatorname{fl}(2s_k),\quad t_k=\operatorname{fl}(q_{k+1}-q_k),\quad f_k=\operatorname{fl}(6t_k)
$$
in that order. Copy $c_k=\widehat h_{k+1}$ for $k<n$. On failure return
`assembly-range-failure(k,operation)`. Let $T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$
have diagonal $d_k$, adjacent off-diagonal entries $c_k$, and zero entries
elsewhere; represent it by these three diagonals, not a dense array. Let the
stored right-hand side be $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_n)^T$.

Factor $T$ with a real lower bidiagonal factor, stored as diagonal
$\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n$ and subdiagonal $e_1,\ldots,e_{n-1}$. For
$k=1,\ldots,n$ in order, set $p_1=d_1$ by exact copy; for $k>1$ compute
$\zeta_k=\operatorname{fl}(e_{k-1}e_{k-1})$ and
$p_k=\operatorname{fl}(d_k-\zeta_k)$. If either operation fails, return
`factor-range-failure(k,operation)`. If the resulting $p_k$ fails the
published positive-normal pivot test of
[[alg-rounded-cholesky-with-failure-status]], return `invalid-pivot(k,p_k)`.
Otherwise compute
$\ell_k=\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt{p_k})$; on failure or a nonpositive or
nonnormal result return `factor-range-failure(k,operation)`. For $k<n$ compute
$e_k=\operatorname{fl}(c_k/\ell_k)$ and return the same indexed factor
status on failure.

Solve $Lz=f$ by forward substitution in increasing index order: set
$z_1=\operatorname{fl}(f_1/\ell_1)$; for $k>1$, compute
$a=\operatorname{fl}(e_{k-1}z_{k-1})$,
$b=\operatorname{fl}(f_k-a)$, and $z_k=\operatorname{fl}(b/\ell_k)$.
Solve $L^T\widehat m=z$ in decreasing order: set
$\widehat m_n=\operatorname{fl}(z_n/\ell_n)$; for $k<n$, compute
$a=\operatorname{fl}(e_k\widehat m_{k+1})$,
$b=\operatorname{fl}(z_k-a)$, and
$\widehat m_k=\operatorname{fl}(b/\ell_k)$. At the first failed operation
return `solve-range-failure(direction,k,operation)`. These are separate
multiply, subtract, and divide operations; no fused multiply-add is used.
Set $\widehat M_1=\widehat M_r=0$ and copy the interior vector
$\widehat M_{k+1}=\widehat m_k$.

Compute the rounded residual in increasing row order. Within row $k$, form
the products $T_{kj}\widehat m_j$ for existing columns $j$ in increasing
column order, and add them sequentially from an exact zero accumulator to
obtain $\widehat v_k$. Then compute
$\widehat w_k=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat v_k-f_k)$. Return the first
`residual-range-failure(k,j,operation)` if any operation fails. Structural
zero entries are omitted; all included products, additions, and the final
subtraction use the operationwise model.

The certificate calculations that follow are exact rational arithmetic on
the finite binary values and the rational $u$; they are not rounded
floating-point calculations. Define
$$
F_1=\sum_{k=1}^n|d_k|+2\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}|c_k|,\quad X_1=\sum_{k=1}^n|\widehat m_k|,\quad Y_1=\sum_{k=1}^n|f_k|,\quad V_1=\sum_{k=1}^n|\widehat v_k|,\quad W_1=\sum_{k=1}^n|\widehat w_k|
$$
and
$$
g_n=\frac{1+6u}{1-(n-1)u}-1,\qquad C=W_1+g_nF_1X_1+u(V_1+Y_1).
$$
Form the exact natural-cubic matrix $A$ and right-hand side $b$ for the
original stored data as in
[[thm-natural-cubic-interpolant-exists-uniquely-at-distinct-knots]]:
$A_{kk}=2(h_k+h_{k+1})$, $A_{k,k+1}=A_{k+1,k}=h_{k+1}$, and
$b_k=6((y_{k+2}-y_{k+1})/h_{k+1}-(y_{k+1}-y_k)/h_k)$, with only existing
interior entries included; represent $A$ by its three diagonals and compute
the following row quantities as a stream, without allocating dense matrices.
Compute
$$
\alpha=\max_k\sum_j|A_{kj}-T_{kj}|,\quad \beta=\max_k|b_k-f_k|,\quad Q=\max_k|\widehat m_k|,\quad \delta=\min_{1\le k\le n}(h_k+h_{k+1}),\quad H=\max_{1\le i<r}h_i,
$$
and
$$
B=\frac{H^2}{8\delta}(C+\alpha Q+\beta).
$$
All denominators are positive: $h_i>0$, $\delta>0$, and
$1-(n-1)u>0$. Return `success(\widehat M,C,\alpha,\beta,B)`. If a
resource-limited implementation cannot complete the exact rational
certificate, it may return `certificate-resource-failure`, which carries no
certified $B$.

For $r\ge3$, associate to the returned vector $\widehat M$ the piecewise
cubic reconstruction on each $[x_i,x_{i+1}]$ given by
$$
\widehat s_i(x)=\frac{\widehat M_i(x_{i+1}-x)^3+\widehat M_{i+1}(x-x_i)^3}{6h_i}+\left(y_i-\frac{\widehat M_i h_i^2}{6}\right)\frac{x_{i+1}-x}{h_i}+\left(y_{i+1}-\frac{\widehat M_{i+1}h_i^2}{6}\right)\frac{x-x_i}{h_i}.
$$
This reconstruction interpolates the stored data and need not be $C^1$ at an interior knot;
it is a piecewise cubic reconstruction, not necessarily a natural spline.
The certificate concerns exact evaluation of these pieces. Any floating-point
evaluation of them needs a separate piece-evaluation error allowance.

Let $r\ge3$, $n=r-2$, and use the stored input data, arithmetic model and
algorithm of
[[alg-natural-cubic-tridiagonal-cholesky-with-residual-certificate]]. If
assembly succeeds, its stored symmetric tridiagonal matrix $T$ is positive
definite. On every full successful call, the algorithm returns
$\operatorname{success}(\widehat M,C,\alpha,\beta,B)$. Let
$\widehat m=(\widehat M_2,\ldots,\widehat M_{r-1})$ be the interior
subvector, let $f$ be the stored right-hand side, and let $\widehat w$ be the
computed rounded residual vector from the algorithm's residual-evaluation
step. Then
$$
\|T\widehat m-f\|_\infty\le C.
$$
For $v\in\mathbb R^n$, the notation here is
$\|v\|_\infty:=\max_{1\le k\le n}|v_k|$.
Thus $e=T\widehat m-f$ is an exact right-hand-side perturbation satisfying
$T\widehat m=f+e$ and $\|e\|_\infty\le C$. This absolute residual
certificate remains valid when $\widehat m=0$ or $f=0$.

The algorithm's factorization and two substitutions are the successful
executions of the published dense rounded Cholesky and triangular-substitution
procedures on the same stored $T$ and $f$, after omitting only exact-zero
operations. Their failure tests retain the published positive-normal pivot
and operationwise range rules. Exact positive definiteness does not guarantee
rounded success.

Write $\widehat L$ and $z$ for the factor and forward-solve vector computed in
this execution. There are additional conditional backward-error statements.
If
$(n+3)u<1$, lower bidiagonal $D_1$ and upper bidiagonal $D_2$ satisfy
$$
(\widehat L+D_1)z=f,\qquad (\widehat L^T+D_2)\widehat m=z,\qquad |D_1|\le\tau|\widehat L|,\qquad |D_2|\le\tau|\widehat L|^T,\qquad \tau=\frac{(n+3)u}{1-(n+3)u}.
$$
If $(20n+20)u<1/5$, put
$g=(20n+20)u/(1-(20n+20)u)$. For the symmetric factor residual
$E=\widehat L\widehat L^T-T$,
$$
|E|\le100g|\widehat L||\widehat L|^T.
$$
With
$$
J=E+D_1\widehat L^T+\widehat L D_2+D_1D_2,
$$
we have $(T+J)\widehat m=f$ and
$$
|J|\le(100g+2\tau+\tau^2)|\widehat L||\widehat L|^T.
$$
The matrix $J$ need not be symmetric. If also
$100\sqrt n\,g\le1/2$, then
$\|E\|_F\le200\sqrt n\,g\|T\|_F$. The residual certificate above
requires only the algorithm's $(n-1)u<1$ check; it does not require these
stronger factor and triangular-solve conditions.

The finite procedure terminates and uses $O(r)$ floating-point operations,
$O(r)$ stored scalars, $O(r)$ exact rational operations and $O(r)$ stored
rationals. No rational bit-complexity bound is asserted.

Let $r\ge2$, $a\le x_1<\cdots<x_r\le b$, and $y_1,\ldots,y_r\in\mathbb R$. There is exactly one natural cubic spline $s$ on $[a,b]$ with $s(x_i)=y_i$ for each $i$. On each interval $[x_i,x_{i+1}]$ it is the cubic with endpoint values $y_i,y_{i+1}$ and endpoint second derivatives $M_i,M_{i+1}$, where $M_1=M_r=0$ and the interior values solve the positive-definite tridiagonal system
$$h_{i-1}M_{i-1}+2(h_{i-1}+h_i)M_i+h_iM_{i+1}=6\left(\frac{y_{i+1}-y_i}{h_i}-\frac{y_i-y_{i-1}}{h_{i-1}}\right),\quad 2\le i\le r-1,$$
with $h_i=x_{i+1}-x_i>0$. The interpolant is linear outside $[x_1,x_r]$.

Let $x_1<\cdots<x_r$, $r\ge3$, and let $s$ be the natural cubic
interpolant of nodal values $y_i$. Write $h_i=x_{i+1}-x_i$ and
$H=\max_i h_i$. Let $A$ be the $(r-2)\times(r-2)$ interior coefficient
matrix in the system of
[[thm-natural-cubic-interpolant-exists-uniquely-at-distinct-knots]], and
let $b$ be its right-hand side. Put
$$\delta=\min_{2\le i\le r-1}(h_{i-1}+h_i)>0.$$
For any proposed nodal second derivatives
$\widehat M_1=\widehat M_r=0$, let $\widehat m$ be their interior vector,
let $\rho=A\widehat m-b$ be the exact residual, and let $\widehat s$ be
the piecewise cubic given by the natural piece formula with these second
derivatives and the same values $y_i$. Then, on the knot hull,
$$\|\widehat s-s\|_{L^\infty([x_1,x_r])}\le \frac{H^2}{8\delta}\|\rho\|_\infty.$$
This is a residual-to-function transfer statement; it does not assert that
a particular floating-point solver returns a residual certificate.

derivations.claim: Suppose $r\ge3$. Let $\widehat M$ be the returned vector and $\widehat m=(\widehat M_2,\ldots,\widehat M_{r-1})$ its interior subvector. By [F2] and the exact identity $A\widehat m-b=(T\widehat m-f)+(A-T)\widehat m+(f-b)$, each row satisfies $|(A\widehat m-b)_k|\le |(T\widehat m-f)_k|+\sum_j|A_{kj}-T_{kj}|\,|\widehat m_j|+|f_k-b_k|\le C+\alpha\|\widehat m\|_\infty+\beta$.
